title: Context and token management
task_statement: Budget context and tokens per turn with token counting, compaction, and context editing. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Context window and token counting
components.first_principle: Every input and output token counts toward the context window, so count tokens before you send a turn.
steps: Call the token counting endpoint with the same model ID you plan to use.
Compare the estimated input tokens with your budget for the turn.
Trim the history, tool definitions, or documents when the total is too high.
Send the request when the total fits the window and the budget.
Check the usage fields in the response for the billed counts.
Count prompts again after a model change, because Claude 4.7 and later models use a newer tokenizer.
pros: Token counting is free to use, subject to rate limits.
Counts help with rate limits, costs, and model routing decisions.
A 1M token window is the default for every model that has one, with no beta header.
cons: The count is an estimate, so the billed count can differ by a small amount.
Token counting does not use prompt caching logic.
Claude Haiku 5.5 counts the same text as about 30 percent more tokens than Claude Haiku 4.5.
use_when: A request nears the budget for one turn or the context window.
A model change may change prompt size.
do_not_use_when: A count from a model before Claude Opus 4.7 is reused for Claude Haiku 5.5.
The request includes a server tool such as web search, or the MCP connector, which the endpoint rejects.

constraints.choice: Count tokens before each send to set a per-turn budget.
constraints.combination: Check the higher Claude Haiku 5.5 rate for prompts over 100,000 tokens.

constraints.choice: Use the 1M token window as the default for long inputs on current models.
constraints.combination: Compact or trim the history before the window fills.

constraints.choice: Plan token counting calls within their requests per minute limit.
constraints.combination: Token counting has its own limit, separate from message creation.

constraints.choice: Log the usage fields for each request.

components.name: Compaction of older turns
components.first_principle: Compaction replaces older turns with a summary that Claude writes on the server, so the active context stays small.

nodes.label: Recent turns kept word for word

steps: Use compaction on demand when your app controls when the summary runs.
Send the compact-2026-09-04 beta header and the compaction parameter.
Receive the summary block from the API in the response.
Place the returned block first in messages, in place of the summarized turns.
To keep recent turns word for word, pick a cut point and send the later turns after the block.
Write a custom summarization prompt when the default summary drops a needed detail.
pros: The API writes the summary, so you need no summarization code.
Recent turns can stay word for word.
Compaction in the background keeps the work active while the summary is written.
cons: Compaction is in beta on the listed platforms.
A summary can drop a detail that a later turn needs.
Threshold compaction does not keep recent turns unless your code pauses after compaction.
use_when: A long agent task would exceed the window or lose focus.
The app controls when older turns get summarized.
do_not_use_when: Only large tool results grow, and a rule-based clear fits better.
Exact instructions must stay word for word in every turn. Keep them in the system prompt (Inference).

constraints.choice: Compact older turns to keep the active context small.
constraints.combination: Use context editing for large old tool results.

constraints.choice: Compact before the window fills, not after the request fails.
constraints.combination: Set the trigger with the threshold option.

constraints.choice: Log each compaction block that appears in a response.
constraints.combination: Test each summary against the later turns (Inference).

components.name: Context editing by rule
components.first_principle: Context editing clears old tool results or thinking blocks by rule, so the context shrinks without a summary.

nodes.label: Clear old tool results by threshold

steps: Send the context-management-2025-06-27 beta header with each request.
Add the clear_tool_uses_20250919 strategy to clear old tool results after a threshold.
Add the clear_thinking_20251015 strategy to manage thinking blocks in earlier turns.
Set the keep value for thinking explicitly when code runs on several model tiers.
Keep thinking blocks when cache hits on later turns matter.
Set clear_at_least so each clear removes enough tokens to justify the cache write.
pros: Old tool results leave the context without a summary call.
Retained thinking blocks preserve cache hits on later turns.
Server-side edits apply before the prompt reaches Claude.
cons: A tool result clear or a thinking block clear invalidates the cached prefix from that point.
Client-side edits to earlier turns can invalidate thinking blocks in later turns.
use_when: Agent tasks produce large tool results that are no longer needed.
The app needs a rule-based clear instead of a summary.
do_not_use_when: The task needs the exact content of old tool results later (Inference).
The team needs a summary of the whole conversation, where compaction fits better.

constraints.choice: Clear old tool results to lower the input tokens per turn.
constraints.combination: Set clear_at_least, because each tool result clear invalidates the cached prefix and adds a cache write.

constraints.choice: Check cache reads after each change to an edit rule.
constraints.combination: Use cache diagnostics when cache reads drop.

constraints.choice: Use a threshold so edits run only for long contexts.
constraints.combination: For most long conversations, the docs prefer server-side compaction as the primary strategy.

constraints.choice: Name the strategy version and threshold in code.

components.exam_tie: D2.4. Expect a scenario where old tool results fill the window and the team asks for the smallest fix. (Inference)
components.trap: A second summary call on every turn looks thorough, but a rule-based clear needs no extra call.
components.decision_rule: Clear old tool results by rule. Keep thinking blocks when cache hits matter.
components.exam_tip: If cache reads drop after a clear, check clear_at_least and the keep setting for thinking blocks.

key_facts.text: Context editing is in beta and needs the context-management-2025-06-27 beta header.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The clear_tool_uses_20250919 strategy clears old tool results when context grows beyond a threshold.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The clear_thinking_20251015 strategy manages thinking blocks from earlier assistant turns.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: On Claude Haiku 5.5, server-side context management never invalidates thinking blocks.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: When thinking blocks are cleared, the prompt cache is invalidated from that position.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A clear of tool results invalidates cached prompt prefixes. Use clear_at_least to clear a minimum number of tokens each time.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: For most use cases, server-side compaction is the primary strategy, and context editing gives fine-grained control.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Request near the window or budget?} -->|No| B[Send the request]
  A -->|Yes| C{Large old tool results?}
  C -->|Yes| D[Clear by rule with context editing]
  C -->|No| E{Long history needed as a summary?}
  E -->|Yes| F[Compact with on demand or threshold]
  E -->|No| G[Trim history in app code]
  D --> H[Count tokens before the next call]
  F --> H
  G --> H
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  C[Count tokens first] --> W[Window 1M tokens]
  W --> E[Clear tool results by rule]
  W --> K[Compact older turns]
  K --> R[Keep recent turns word for word]
  E --> T[Keep thinking for cache hits]
  C --> L[Haiku 5.5 higher rate above 100k]
